policies.title: Vietnamese citizenship is outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: A Vietnamese ordinary passport belongs to a Vietnamese citizen and is not classified through the foreigner eVisa or foreign visitor-exemption framework.
conditions: Does not decide a dual national’s document choice, overseas-Vietnamese visa-exemption certificate, residence, departure, security, or individual admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Twelve nationalities: Resolution 44 unilateral visa exemption
policies.summary: The current Resolution 44 policy exempts these nationals from visas for a 45-day stay, regardless of passport type or entry purpose.
conditions: Applies to Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the United Kingdom, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, and Finland, regardless of passport type and entry purpose.

Requires full compliance with Vietnam’s legal entry conditions. The current MOFA table states unilateral-exemption entrants need a passport valid at least six months and at least 30 days outside Viet Nam since their last departure.
British National (Overseas) passport holders are expressly excluded by the MOFA table; this ordinary UK-passport policy does not cover BNO or other special British documents.
Work, residence, overseas-Vietnamese, diplomatic/official, transit, crew, and individual security/admissibility rules remain separate.

policies.title: Twelve nationalities: Resolution 229 visa exemption
policies.summary: The current Resolution 229 policy exempts these nationals from visas for up to 45 days from entry, regardless of passport type, subject to legal entry conditions.
conditions: Applies to Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, Hungary, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, and Switzerland, regardless of passport type.

Maximum stay is 45 days from entry and remains subject to Vietnam’s legal entry conditions. The current MOFA table states unilateral-exemption entrants need a passport valid at least six months and at least 30 days outside Viet Nam since their last departure.
This current 2025-2028 resolution supersedes the expired 2025 Poland/Czechia/Switzerland package-tour pilot for the same ordinary passports; do not retain the expired tour-only condition.
Work, residence, overseas-Vietnamese, diplomatic/official, transit, crew, and individual security/admissibility rules remain separate.

policies.title: Belarus ordinary passports: reciprocal visa exemption
policies.summary: Belarus ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for up to 30 days per stay, capped at 90 days in a calendar year.
conditions: The current MOFA table records 30 days for all passport types and caps ordinary-passport stay at 90 days in a calendar year.
The ordinary-passport agreement is distinct from diplomatic/official rules; purpose, work, residence, security, and admission limitations remain governed by Vietnamese law.

policies.title: Brunei ordinary passports: 14-day visa exemption
policies.summary: Brunei ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for stays up to 14 days.
conditions: The current MOFA table distinguishes 14 days for ordinary Brunei passports from 30 days for diplomatic and official passports.
Does not establish work, residence, diplomatic/official, transit, crew, special-document, security, or individual-admission rights.

policies.title: Ten ordinary passports: bilateral short-stay visa exemptions
policies.summary: These current bilateral instruments give ordinary-passport holders short-stay visa exemption, with duration and purpose conditions varying by nationality.
conditions: Cambodia, Indonesia, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Malaysia, Mongolia, Myanmar, Singapore, and Thailand have 30-day ordinary-passport routes; Kazakhstan is 30 days per entry, capped at 90 days in each 180-day period.

The current MOFA instrument schedule records: Cambodia effective 5 December 2008 (amended 1 January 2010); Indonesia 4 December 2003; Kazakhstan 25 May 2024; Laos 1 July 2004; Malaysia 25 November 2001; Myanmar 26 October 2013 (amended 1 January 2020); Mongolia 6 March 2024; Singapore 1 December 2003; and Thailand 9 July 2000. It identifies Kyrgyzstan as a successor arrangement with the former Soviet agreement, without printing an effective date.

Cambodia, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Laos, Mongolia, Myanmar, and Singapore require at least six months' passport validity. Mongolia, Myanmar, and Singapore exclude income-earning activity; Myanmar also excludes other commercial activity. Malaysia is limited to the listed short-visit purposes; Laos and Indonesia have separate extension/residence rules.

The MOFA table separately records ordinary-passport periods for these bilateral arrangements. Do not generalize diplomatic, official, service, special, crew, ASEAN-official-event, residence, or border-pass rows to ordinary visitor passports.

policies.title: Philippines ordinary passports: 21-day visa exemption
policies.summary: Philippines ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for stays up to 21 days when they hold a passport valid at least six months and an onward or return ticket.
conditions: The current MOFA table records an ordinary-passport exemption of up to 21 days, requiring a passport valid at least six months and a return or onward ticket.
The table separately identifies diplomatic, official, ASEAN-official-event, work, residence, special-document, security, and individual-admission provisions; they are not generalized here.

policies.title: Chile and Panama ordinary passports: 90-day non-remunerated-activity exemptions
policies.summary: Chile and Panama ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for stays up to 90 days when entry is not for income-earning activity.
conditions: The MOFA table records 90-day ordinary-passport exemption for Chile and Panama; the underlying ordinary-passport rules require passports valid at least six months and prohibit entry for income-earning activity.
Do not generalize the diplomatic/official/special, crew, residence, employment, or individual security/admission provisions.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: all-nationalities eVisa
policies.summary: Every other catalog foreign ordinary-passport code can use Vietnam’s nationality-wide electronic-visa route; it is normalized as evisa.
conditions: Available to foreigners outside Viet Nam holding a valid passport or international travel document. The Article 8 visa-class and Article 16 invitation/guarantee rules, including their personal, delegation, diplomatic, residence, and purpose distinctions, remain separate procedures rather than nationality-wide ordinary-passport exclusions.

Valid for at most 90 days, for single or multiple entry. The Ministry of Public Security states that application, issuance, receipt, printing, and fee payment are electronic; an issued eVisa can be printed without collecting a visa at a mission or border gate.

Use only Government-designated international air, land, or sea border gates. The Government Portal confirms the official site publishes the eVisa border-gate list; the pre-arrival declaration is not an ETA or visa-exemption substitute.

Entry and stay remain conditioned on a valid travel document, the stated entry purpose, no suspension/prohibition from entry, and border-control admission. Accommodation providers must make temporary-residence declarations; work, residence, diplomatic/official, crew, border-pass, transit and overseas-Vietnamese certificate routes are distinct.

application.label: Viet Nam E-Visa
steps: Apply personally from outside Viet Nam, accurately complete the eVisa form, and select approved entry/exit border gates.
Pay the non-refundable eVisa fee and receive the result electronically before travel.
Enter and exit only at the designated border gates and comply with temporary-residence declaration and border-control requirements.
